Asking: PriceCharting guide A$69 to A$86, new retail A$129 (US) and A$155.75 (Booktopia). Rate 1 USD = 1.4328 AUD. No Australian or international auction house result found.
lots.working: No SOLD entry in the last 24 months (latest PriceCharting sale is May 2023), so keep and flip are 0. For context only: a sealed copy realistically resells about A$80 to A$100 on old evidence; (A$90 less about 13% fees and A$15 post = A$63) / 2.396 = A$26 would be the flip ceiling if that evidence were current, and buying new from Booktopia at A$155.75 sets the top of what anyone should pay all-in.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification is clear from the photo (gold cartridge cover, Nintendo sleeve), but every sold price is more than 24 months old and the rest is asking or guide data. No auction house record found.

lots.question_for_gowans: Is the shrink-wrap fully intact with no tears, and are the corners of the sleeve and book uncrushed?

lots.condition: Appears sealed in shrink-wrap; only the front is shown, so edges, spine and back are unverified.

lots.what_it_is: German-made Edison-style 2-minute cylinder phonograph c.1905-10, black japanned bedplate with gilt and red decoration and a small gold shield transfer (script name partly legible, possibly Puck), on oak base with bentwood oak dome cover, aluminium horn, with 3 Edison cylinders (including 13783 Harry Lauder 'He Was Very Kind To Me' and 10347).

SOLD. Page opened. Genuine Edison Home phonograph in oak case with aluminium horn and a collection of cylinders, no condition report. Category guide: a genuine Edison, normally worth more than a German copy, yet it made only GBP 190 hammer, which is a useful reality check on the top end. Rate 1 GBP = 1.8983 AUD (open.er-api.com, 14 Oct 2026).

lots.guide_summary: A$361 to A$1,146, all sold, none the same machine. Two close German Puck/Carette open-works machines made A$573 and A$1,146 at a US specialist collection sale (Jul 2026); a French Phenix board-and-cover machine made A$573; a genuine Edison Home with aluminium horn made A$361 hammer in the UK (Aug 2025). No unsold or asking entries survive. No Australian auction result found. Rates: 1 USD = 1.4328 AUD, 1 GBP = 1.8983 AUD.
lots.working: No SOLD entry is the same machine (the Puck open-works and Phenix are different models, the Toovey's lot is a genuine Edison), so per the rules keep and flip are 0. For context only: if the machine is complete and runs, the evidence suggests about A$350 to A$600 in Australia; the cheapest relevant sale (A$361) / 1.198 = A$301 would be a keep ceiling if it were a true match, and (A$450 resale less 13% fees and A$60 freight = A$331) / 2.396 = A$138 a flip ceiling.
lots.confidence_reason: Shield transfer only partly legible (possibly Puck), maker unconfirmed, running condition unknown, and no same-machine sold result found. WebSearch budget ran out, so no Australian house results could be searched this pass.
lots.dropped_entries: None of the researcher's entries dropped; both Donley Puck lots confirmed (US$800 and US$400, 30 Jul 2026). Added Donley lot 3246 (Phenix) and Toovey's lot 2550 (Edison Home), both pages opened. Donley lot 3244 (Puck lyre base) showed no sold price, not used.
lots.question_for_gowans: Does the motor wind and run, and does the mandrel turn? Is there a reproducer and a horn crane or support (none is clearly visible), and does the aluminium horn fit the machine? What is the name on the small gold shield transfer? Do the bentwood cover and base fit together, and are the 3 cylinders free of cracks and mould?
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 crop: black japanned motor housing with gilt scroll and red-and-gold lining, Edison-style feedscrew carriage with a brass ball weight, key-wind spring handle, cylinder mandrel. Small gold shield transfer at lower left of bedplate with a script name partly legible (could read Puck), not readable with certainty. Oak base with moulded edge; separate bentwood oak dome cover with metal handle. Large spun aluminium horn. Three cylinder boxes: 'Edison Record' labels, 13783 (Harry Lauder, He Was Very Kind To Me, lettering also seen on the cylinder rim) and 10347; third label faded.
lots.condition: Looks complete and tidy in photos with bright decoration; running condition, reproducer and horn support unverified. Cylinders' boxes worn.

lots.what_it_is: German-made toy magic lantern outfit c.1890-1910 for the English market, in its fitted crackle-painted wooden box: nickel bell-shaped lamp housing on a wooden panel, cast iron scroll bracket, nickel and brass lens tube, brass oil font, German instruction sheet in the lid, plus strips of printed 'Ticket for Entertainment with the Magic Lantern' tickets. No slides seen; maker not seen.

lots.guide_summary: A$86 to A$462 across close entries: sold A$86 (US, Sep 2026), A$430 (US, 2010) and A$462 incl. premium (Germany, date unknown); unsold at a A$143 start (US, Aug 2026). The two recent US results (sold US$60, unsold at US$100) point to the low end for a slideless box outfit; the higher prices were for named makers with slides. A 2007 Plank sale at A$1,003 is a category guide only and is outside the range. No asking entries. No Australian result found. Rates 1 USD = 1.4328 AUD, 1 EUR = 1.6039 AUD.
lots.working: Only one SOLD entry in the last 24 months (Donley US$60 = A$86, Sep 2026), and it is a close match, not the same item, so keep and flip are 0 under the rules. For context: A$86 / 1.198 = A$71 would be the keep ceiling if it were a true match; a flip would be (about A$120 resale less 13% fees and A$25 post = A$79) / 2.396 = A$33, which is barely worth it.
lots.confidence_reason: Maker not seen, no slides, lantern shown partly dismantled, and only one recent close sale (low) plus one recent unsold. Older higher sales are for better named outfits.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher's Donley p=47875 'ASKING, snippet only' entry was wrong: I opened it and it SOLD for US$60 on 26 Sep 2026, so moved to SOLD. Theriault's dates (2010-03-28, 2007-05-05) confirmed from page data. Leitz date still unconfirmed. No entries dropped.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there a maker's name or trademark on the lamp housing, lens tube or instruction sheet? Are there any glass slides with it? Does the lamp housing have its chimney, and is the lens glass present and uncracked?
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 crop: printed tickets reading 'Ticket for Entertainment with the Magic Lantern' (misspelt, typical of German toys made for the English market). Photo 2: nickel bell-shaped lamp housing fixed to a black panel with orange edge, ornate cast iron scroll bracket, nickel lens tube with brass ends, brass oil font; German-language instruction sheet glued in the lid (text not legible enough to read a maker). Photo 3: black crackle-painted pine box with lock escutcheon and side handles, worn edges. No slides visible.
lots.condition: Box worn with paint loss on edges; metal parts tarnished but appear intact; completeness (chimney, slides) unverified.
